text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH p99 latency alert for /v1/stream-generate (pool=eu-prod-XL). p95 jumped from ~1.1s to ~3.8s, p99 from ~3.4s to ~18.2s. Streaming stalls reported. queue_depth=1200 (sustained), inflight_streams=340, backend_errors=0.
maria: i'm looking — paging @nate-oncall. any quick context on recent deploys?
devin: no user deploys. I see a routing spike: 2x increase in requests to eu-prod-XL starting +00:12 UTC, and a lot of KV cache cold-path misses. cache_hit_rate dropped 72% -> 21%.
cheng: autoscaler logs: many warmup-handshakes timed out, nodes provisioning succeeded but runtime warmup (kv prefill + tensor init) is taking ~35-60s per replica. handshake_delay histogram tail is spiking.
maria: ok, primary hypothesis: burst -> cache cold-path -> longer warmup -> pool handshake backlog -> queue amplification.
julie-cs: customers affected: acme-inc and beaconlabs seeing streaming timeouts and partial responses. CS notified, collecting session ids.
devin: metrics + tiny sample traces: attached flame shows long wait in "kv_prefill" and then stalls inside stream write loop. Example trace id=trace_0cd4a: 
```
{"span":"kv_prefill","dur_ms":41200}
{"span":"prepare_stream","dur_ms":15800}
{"span":"write_chunk","dur_ms":9800}
```

maria: mitigation plan: 1) divert 40% of traffic for this route to fallback model variant (smaller quantized) to reduce warmup cost, 2) manual scale +4 replicas to eu-prod-XL, 3) apply temporary per-key rate-limit /burst to heavy customers, 4) enable prewarm flag for new nodes. I'll execute 1 and 2 now.
devin: pushing routing change — creating rollout: 
```
api.post('/routing/override', {route:'/v1/stream-generate', pct:40, variant:'gpt-quant-sm'} )
```

cheng: running manual scale: 
```
infra scale-pool --pool eu-prod-XL --delta 4 --reason "manual burst mitigation"
```

maria: routing change in prod -> diverted 40% to gpt-quant-sm. queue_depth dropped to ~520 within 90s. p95 dropped to ~1.2s, p99 now ~5.8s (still elevated). :eyes:
julie-cs: CS: acme-inc confirms fewer timeouts, one still seeing stalls on long streaming sessions.
devin: started targeted trace capture for sessions with >10s stall. grabbing top 20 traces now.
cheng: found an autoscaler regression: after last runtime patch the warmup handshake concurrency default was lowered from 12 -> 4 which causes serial warmups under bursts. when many replicas provision simultaneously we hit a bottleneck in the KV prefill worker pool. Filed quick bug: RN-3987.
maria: good catch. short-term config change: bump warmup_concurrency to 10 and increase handshake timeout to 90s. cheng can you patch config?
cheng: applying patch to staging then prod: 
```
set-config --path /runtime/warmup_concurrency --value 10
set-config --path /runtime/warmup_timeout_s --value 90
deploy-config --env prod --component runtime
```

nate-oncall: i'm taking the oncall handoff to monitor. what's the expected rollback window if this makes things worse?
maria: rollback plan: revert routing override + scale down manually by 4, and restore warmup_concurrency=4. but do not scale down until p99 < 2s for 10m.
cheng: config patch deployed to prod at +00:47 UTC. warmup concurrency increased, prefill worker utilization improved immediately. new traces show kv_prefill reduced from ~41s -> ~9s for warmed flows.
devin: after config + routing: queue_depth ~180, p95 ~0.95s, p99 ~1.8s. streaming stall rate down 95%.
julie-cs: notifying impacted customers with timeline and mitigation steps. will follow up on session-level recovery and refunds if needed.
maria: creating follow-up action items: 1) RN-3987 autoscaler warmup regression (priority P0), 2) add burst-shedder for new-pool handshake, 3) add dashboard for kv_cache_hit_rate per-pool, 4) customer postmortem draft.
nate-oncall: taking ownership for night monitoring. i'll watch the rollout and escalate if p99 > 2.5s for >5m. paging channel mutation: @oncall-rotation updated.
maria: thanks team. leaving this thread for the night shift. final note: no data exfiltration, only latency/customer impact. will assemble incident timeline in postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
